transcript.content: Hello. What brings you in to see me today?

Hello. Well, what finally got me to make an appointment is that my concentration has gotten pretty unreliable lately. I’ll be at the clinic reviewing a patient's chart, or even just at home laying out a watercolor wash, and suddenly I realize I’ve read the same line three times. My mind just keeps wandering off to everything that could possibly go wrong.
About how long have you been experiencing these worries and trouble concentrating?
It's been, well, since I started the formal retirement process. That was about a year and three months ago.
Aside from the worries, have you been feeling down, depressed, or hopeless most days?
No, not really. I mean, I wouldn't say I feel depressed or hopeless. It's more just this constant... buzzing in my head about all the things I need to sort out, rather than feeling sad or down.
Do you find it difficult to control or stop these worries once they start?

Yes, I really do. I try to... well, I try to reason with myself the same way I would with a nervous patient. But it doesn't seem to work. One concern just leads right into the next, and instead of just letting it go, I usually end up checking my emails, reviewing my notes, or asking the same questions all over again.
Are these worries mainly focused on your retirement, or do you find yourself worrying about a variety of different everyday topics?

It's a mix of things, really. My mind just keeps circling around all sorts of issues. I mean, I worry about whether my old patients are being looked after properly by the new team, and I stress over whether the practice handoff is financially sound. But it's also personal stuff... like whether I’ll just become useless once I’m fully retired. So it covers a lot of ground, and honestly, the amount of worry feels out of proportion even to me.
Along with this constant worry, have you been feeling restless, keyed up, or on edge?

I wouldn't say I feel restless or keyed up, no. I haven't really noticed feeling on edge like that. It's really just the thoughts in my head that won't stop, rather than a physical feeling of being restless.
Have you noticed any changes or difficulties with your sleep?

Yeah, my sleep has definitely been affected. Most nights I get into bed feeling pretty tired, but... well, as soon as the house gets quiet, my mind just starts up. I start replaying all the patient transfers, going over the money details for the practice... it just keeps going. And even when I finally manage to get to sleep, I'm usually waking up around four or five in the morning, and I just feel like I never really settled or got a good rest.
Have you been experiencing any physical muscle tension, such as stiffness, tightness, or soreness in your neck, shoulders, or jaw?

No, I haven't really noticed any muscle tension. My neck and shoulders feel fine, and I don't think I've been clenching my jaw or anything like that. Like I said, it's mostly just the thoughts racing in my head, not really physical aches or stiffness.
Have you been finding yourself getting tired or fatigued more easily than usual?

Yes, I have. By midafternoon, I just feel completely worn out. It's a kind of tired that a nap or taking it easy in the morning just doesn't seem to fix. Simple things, you know, like weeding out in the garden or even just standing at my easel to paint... they just feel a lot heavier and take more out of me than they used to.
